title: Cupid (Sam Cooke song)

{{Short description|1961 single by Sam Cooke}} {{Infobox song | name = Cupid | cover = Cupid Sam Cooke.jpg | alt = | type = single | artist = [[Sam Cooke]] | album = [[The Best of Sam Cooke]] | B-side = Farewell My Darling | released = {{Start date|1961|05|16}} | recorded = April 14, 1961 | studio = [[RCA Records#RCA Victor Music Center of the World, Hollywood|RCA]] (Hollywood, California) | venue = | genre = [[Rhythm and blues]] | length = {{Duration|m=2|s=30}} | label = [[RCA Victor]] | writer = [[Sam Cooke]] | producer = [[Hugo & Luigi]] | prev_title = That's It, I Quit, I'm Moving On | prev_year = 1961 | next_title = Feel It | next_year = 1961 }} "'''Cupid'''" is a song by the American singer [[Sam Cooke]], released on May 16, 1961. It charted at number 17 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and number 20 on the [[R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B Sides]] chart; the track performed best in the [[United Kingdom]], peaking at number seven on the [[UK Singles Chart]]. The song is featured on Cooke's greatest hits album, ''[[The Best of Sam Cooke]]'' (1962). ==History== Cooke's producers had asked him to write a song for [[Sandy Stewart (singer)|Sandy Stewart]], who they had seen on ''[[The Perry Como Show]]''—but once they heard her sing more than one sing, they kept "Cupid" for Cooke himself.{{sfn|Guralnick|2005|pp=362-364}} The song was recorded at Cooke's debut session at [[RCA Records]] in Los Angeles, produced by Cooke and [[Hugo & Luigi]], but only [[Luigi Creatore]] was able to attend as co-producer [[Hugo Peretti]] was afraid of flying.{{sfn|Wolff|1995|pp=236-237}} [[René Hall]] arranged the piece with French horn and strings.{{sfn|Wolff|1995|p=237}} Personnel included Cooke's session regulars Clifton White and Hall on guitar, Clifford Hills on bass, [[Earl Palmer]] on drums and Joseph Gibbons on guitar and banjo.{{cite AV media notes |title=[[Portrait of a Legend: 1951–1964]] |others=[[Sam Cooke]] |date=2026 |pages=7, 16, 20-21 |type=Liner notes |publisher=[[ABKCO]] |id=9872418}} Cooke's original idea{{sfn|Wolff|1995|p=237}} was to bring in the Sims Twins, the gospel duo of Bobbie and Kenneth Sims, to perform backing vocals mimicking the sound of a bow shooting an arrow.{{sfn|Guralnick|2005|pp=362-364}} The final version was chosen after seven takes.{{sfn|Wolff|1995|pp=236-237}} Cooke left for a tour of the [[West Indies]] shortly after completing the recording.{{sfn|Wolff|1995|p=238}} ==Reception== An [[AllMusic]] critic described the track as a "perfect pop song" which combines "Latin, R&B, jazz, and mainstream pop elements".{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/song/cupid-mt0014588548|title=Cupid - Sam Cooke|last=Janovitz|first=Bill|publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=September 5, 2014}} ==Charts and certifications== "Cupid" was ranked at number 452 in ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine's list of the "[[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|500 Greatest Songs of All Time]]" in 2004 and at number 458 in 2010. ===Weekly charts=== {{col-begin|width=67%}} {{col-2}} {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !scope="col" style="width:17em;"|Chart (1961 - extract: "Cupid" is a song by the American singer Sam Cooke, released on May 16, 1961. It charted at number 17 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 20 on the Hot R&B Sides chart; the track performed best in the United Kingdom, peaking at number seven on the UK Singles Chart. The song is featured on Cooke's greatest hits album, The Best of Sam Cooke (1962).
